bricks.headline: Global Landmine Casualties Reach Five-Year High
bricks.summary: Landmine casualties around the world have reached their highest level in five years. Most of the deaths occurred in Southeast Asia. In Syria, nearly 1,000 children were killed or injured by left-over explosives.
bricks.whyItMatters: Leftover landmines endanger everyday citizens and children long after armed conflicts end, restricting safe travel and farming.
bricks.explainer: A new report from a global landmine monitor shows that injuries and deaths from landmines reached a five-year high last year. Researchers found that 84 percent of all landmine deaths occurred in Southeast Asia, with nations like Myanmar heavily affected. In Syria, two years after intense fighting ended, unexploded weapons have harmed or killed nearly 1,000 children. Experts warn that buried explosives remain active for decades after active combat stops. Civilians walking to school, working on farms, or traveling between villages face constant hazards from these hidden weapons, making post-war recovery extremely dangerous for local communities.

bricks.headline: Cuba Life Expectancy Drops for First Time Since 1950
bricks.summary: Life expectancy in Cuba has dropped for the first time in over 70 years. The World Health Organization says average life expectancy fell from 78.8 years to 74.4 years. The country is suffering from a deep economic crisis.
bricks.whyItMatters: Declining life expectancy shows how severe economic distress and shortages directly worsen everyday health and survival for an entire nation.
bricks.explainer: The World Health Organization reported that life expectancy in Cuba has fallen for the first time since record-keeping began in 1950. Speaking in Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that average life expectancy dropped from 78.8 years in 2020 down to 74.4 years in 2025. The sharp decline reflects the impact of a severe economic crisis gripping the island nation. Shortages of fuel, medical supplies, and basic necessities have strained the healthcare system and affected living conditions across the country. Official statistics highlight how prolonged financial hardship is directly impacting public health and longevity for ordinary citizens in Cuba.
